name: IGF-1 DES
route: Injection in research and gray-market use
status: Never approved for human use; sold as a research chemical and black-market product; banned in sport by WADA
mechanism: IGF-1 missing its first three amino acids, so it binds IGF-binding proteins poorly and acts about ten times more strongly in cell studies

article.summary: IGF-1 DES is a truncated, more potent form of insulin-like growth factor 1 sold for muscle growth. It was never approved for people, can lower blood sugar strongly, and is banned in sport.
article.takeaway: IGF-1 DES, or des(1-3)IGF-1, is a natural variant of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) that lacks three amino acids at one end. That change lets it escape the binding proteins that normally restrain IGF-1, making it about ten times more potent than IGF-1 in cultured cells.[^1] It has never been approved for human use, yet it is sold on the black market to bodybuilders, and analyses of such products have found lower-quality, oxidized material.[^2] In animals, IGF-1 variants like this lowered blood sugar more strongly and for longer than IGF-1 itself.[^3] WADA prohibits IGF-1 and its analogues at all times.[^4]
glance: Injection in gray-market use; no approved dosing
Cell and animal studies; no human trials found[^1]
Prohibited at all times (WADA lists IGF-1 and its analogues)[^4]

blocks.text: IGF-1 is made mainly by the liver in response to growth hormone and drives growth in muscle, bone and other tissues. In blood, most IGF-1 is held by IGF-binding proteins, which limit how much is active. Des(1-3)IGF-1 lacks the first three amino acids (Gly-Pro-Glu) and has been isolated from human brain, bovine colostrum and porcine uterus. Without the glutamate at position 3 it binds those proteins poorly, so more of it reaches the IGF-1 receptor.[^1]

Research on des(1-3)IGF-1 is almost entirely in cultured cells and animals. It is roughly 10-fold more potent than IGF-1 at stimulating growth of cultured cells, and in animals the extra potency persists after injection, with selective effects on gut tissue.[^1] A 1996 review said its clinical uses had not been evaluated.[^1] The searches for this entry found no human trial of injected des(1-3)IGF-1, so muscle-building claims have no human evidence.
The IGF-1 medicine approved for people is mecasermin, used for a rare growth disorder. See [mecasermin](/peptides/mecasermin).

items: **Low blood sugar:** in pigs and marmosets, IGF-1 variants that bind poorly to binding proteins lowered glucose 2- to 3-fold more potently than IGF-1 and for much longer, and des(1-3)IGF-1 was the strongest[^3]

**Cancer questions:** higher circulating IGF-1 is linked to higher risk of prostate and premenopausal breast cancer in pooled studies; whether analogs used by athletes carry the same risk is unknown[^5]

**Quality:** anti-doping labs found many oxidized, lower-quality peptide forms in black-market IGF-1 analog products[^2], and a related case found a laboratory version of IGF-1 LR3 carrying an extra purification tag in an injection vial[^6]
**No human safety or dosing data** exist

blocks.text: Des(1-3)IGF-1 has never been approved for human use. WADA prohibits IGF-1 and its analogues at all times,[^4] and anti-doping laboratories have validated methods to detect it.[^2] It does not appear in any category of the FDA's May 2026 list of bulk substances nominated for pharmacy compounding.[^7]

IGF-1 DES is a laboratory tool with strong effects in cells and animals. It has no human trials, a known tendency to lower blood sugar in animals, an unsettled cancer question and unreliable black-market supply. Athletes subject to testing should treat it as banned.

evidence.label: Preclinical: cell and animal studies only
evidence.text: The evidence is cell culture and animal work.[^1][^3] No human trial of the compound was found.

faq.q: Is IGF-1 DES the same as IGF-1 LR3?
faq.a: No. Both are engineered IGF-1 variants that bind IGF-binding proteins poorly, but they differ in structure. See [IGF-1 LR3](/peptides/igf-1-lr3).

faq.q: Why would it affect blood sugar?
faq.a: IGF-1 can lower blood glucose, and variants that escape binding proteins did so more strongly and for longer in animal tests.[^3]
Yes. WADA prohibits IGF-1 and its analogues at all times.[^4]
